references.text: The prohibition against misusing the Lord's name in the Ten Commandments, which forms the basis for the death penalty for blasphemy.
Reiteration of the command not to misuse the Lord's name, with a warning that the Lord will not hold innocent anyone who misuses his name.
The context where the congregation is commanded to take the blasphemer outside the camp and stone him.
The execution of the judgment where the Israelites stoned the blasphemer as the Lord had commanded Moses.
Naboth is falsely accused of having mocked God and the king, and is stoned as a result.
A parallel law concerning stoning where both foreigner and native are treated equally in case of violation.
The one who sins with a high hand mocks the Lord and shall be cut off from the people.
The high priest accuses Jesus of blasphemy and declares him guilty of death.
The Jews seek to stone Jesus because they believe he is mocking God by making himself equal to God.
Stephen is accused of speaking blasphemous words against Moses and God, which leads to his stoning.
The high priest tears his clothes and accuses Jesus of blasphemy during the trial.
